meeting_header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Location: Zoom
Organizer: Maya Chen (Redwood)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Alex Rivera (Cerulean CTO); Priya Shah (Cerulean Infra); Jonas Meier (Cerulean Solutions); Sara Delgado (Cerulean Security); Mike Tan (Cerulean Procurement)
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Cerulean Dataworks to scope an integrator-led pilot for hybrid GPU onramp and a private VPC deployment. Main concerns: data residency, KMS integration, latency SLOs for 2k token workflows, and procurement timeline. Agreed next steps include security docs, pilot SOW draft, and a short benchmark run with representative dataset.
topics: High-level product fit (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
Pilot scope and timelines (SOW, pricing, benchmarks)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood partner team. Liam's my SE, he'll take deeper tech questions.
[00:10] Alex Rivera: Hey Maya, thanks. Alex here, CTO at Cerulean. We — we run a lot of inference workloads for customers, and we're exploring partners to help speed up hybrid onramp.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Priya, infra lead. main things for us are VPC, private key management, and no data exfil.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Great, thanks. quick high-level from Redwood: we offer hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deploy (VPC / on-prem). For partners like integrators, the typical pattern is — uh — a dedicated or private control plane depending on compliance.
[00:45] Jonas Meier: When you say private, do you mean we run everything behind our firewall or Redwood still touches model binary?
[00:52] Liam O'Connor: Good q. there's two modes: Private control plane with customer-managed networking — Redwood control plane endpoints talk over mTLS but compute can be inside your VPC. Alternatively we can ship an on-prem package for air-gapped. both supported.
[01:10] Sara Delgado: How does key management work? our legal team requires BYOK / HSM.
[01:18] Maya Chen: We integrate with KMS/HSMs — customers can bring their own keys. sometimes it's KMS through cloud provider or customer HSM with integration. i will send our KMS integration doc.
[01:30] Alex Rivera: Cool. also curious about audit logs and retention. we need full request logs for 13 months.
[01:38] Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console can stream audit logs to your SIEM and we support configurable retention. slight caveat: token-level logs are redacted depending on config — we'll share specifics.
[01:50] Mike Tan: From procurement, pricing model? we need predictable committed pricing for pilot + an enterprise option.
[01:57] Maya Chen: For pilots we usually do a committed reserved capacity block or trial credits on hosted. for long-term integrator deals we can scope Dedicated with monthly commits. i'll put numbers in the SOW draft.
[02:10] Alex Rivera: On perf: our main workload is document ingestion + Q&A, about 2k token sequences, p95 latency target around 350ms. is that realistic?
[02:21] Liam O'Connor: 350ms p95 for 2k context is tight, depends on model and quantization. With our runtime + model variant selection — e.g., quantized 8-bit LLMs and per-request KV caching — in Dedicated setups we've hit ~300-400ms on Ampere-class; but i'd want to run a benchmark. we'll include continuous batching config and kernel selection tuning.
[02:50] Jonas Meier: you mentioned KV cache — we've heard that can speed up conversational workloads but not sure how it works across distributed nodes.
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: right, KV cache stores prefix key/values to skip recomputation. across nodes we either shard the cache or use a sticky routing policy to keep session affinity. there are tradeoffs: stickiness increases headroom but less global throughput.
[03:18] Alex Rivera: any known integration pain points with existing SI? we use a mix of Kubernetes and some on-prem VMs.
[03:25] Liam O'Connor: kube is very common — our deployment abstraction maps to k8s primitives, and we support both node-bound GPUs and isolated bare-metal. On-prem air-gapped needs additional packaging.
[03:40] Priya Shah: Network egress — we need to ensure no model payloads leave the region, we operate in eu-west.
[03:47] Maya Chen: region pinning is supported; routing policies can restrict routing to eu regions and have fallbacks only within approved pools.
[03:55] Sara Delgado: Posters to SOC2 and ISO?
[04:00] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood is SOC 2 type II. i'll share the certs and the attestation.
[04:07] Alex Rivera: ok great. i wanted to call out our success criteria: 1) <400ms p95 on representative 2k workflows; 2) no PCI/PHI data stored; 3) audit logs available; 4) pilot pricing within our commit band.
[04:21] Maya Chen: perfect, that's helpful. timeline-wise what are you thinking?
[04:25] Alex Rivera: we'd like a 4-week pilot starting asap, preferably before end of month. procurement timelines are tight.
[04:31] Mike Tan: yes procurement can turn quickly if we have a SOW and security pack.
[04:36] Maya Chen: we'll aim to send SOW + pricing by EOD tomorrow and security pack by Thursday.
[04:42] Liam O'Connor: for the bench test i propose a short synthetic run plus a small representative dataset you provide. we'll share an inference config (batch size, kv-cache settings, quantization profile).
[04:55] Jonas Meier: what's the expected delta between hosted trial perf vs dedicated?
[05:02] Liam O'Connor: typically dedicated lowers jitter and improves p95 by 10–25% depending on variance. hosted is good for feature eval but for strict SLOs dedicated/private is recommended. transcription note: sometimes product names get munged — e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" was transcribed earlier as "Redwood dedikate".
[05:30] Alex Rivera: any compliance gotchas for EU data residency?
[05:35] Maya Chen: we can enforce region restrictions; for fully private workloads we can run compute in your VPC so data never leaves region.
[05:45] Priya Shah: curious about model lifecycle and rollouts — we need controlled canaries for model updates.
[05:51] Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, automatic fallbacks. you can pin model versions and route traffic rules by percentage.
[06:05] Alex Rivera: sweet. procurement will want to see sample contract language about liability and uptime. what's your SLA?
[06:12] Maya Chen: for Dedicated we provide SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in enterprise contracts; we'll include SLA clauses in the SOW.
[06:20] Sara Delgado: is there a way to demo the audit logs being pushed to our SIEM?
[06:25] Liam O'Connor: yes we can set up a short integration to forward logs to a Sumo/Graylog endpoint or show a sample.
[06:33] Mike Tan: we also evaluate competitors — Lambda Labs and direct NVIDIA appliances — what makes Redwood different?
[06:40] Maya Chen: main differentiation is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, developer-first APIs, and tooling for cost/perf optimization (batching, kv-caching, quantization recommendations). Also our partner program supports integrator workflows and hybrid pilots.
[07:00] Alex Rivera: any expected infra changes on our side for a pilot?
[07:05] Liam O'Connor: for private/VPC mode you'll need peering or a private endpoint; for on-prem we ship a package. minimal infra changes otherwise — mostly routing and IAM.
[07:20] Jonas Meier: about telemetry — does Redwood collect PII in logs? we need log redaction controls.
[07:26] Maya Chen: yes, we have redaction and tokenization options; we can enable automatic redaction for sensitive fields.
[07:35] Alex Rivera: ok let's talk pilot details — volume, traffic patterns, and acceptance tests.
[07:40] Liam O'Connor: propose 2-week benchmark with 100 rps sustained, mixed seq lengths up to 2k tokens, and a functional QA for correctness. acceptance: p95 under 400ms and <2% error rate.
[07:56] Priya Shah: 100 rps sustained might be high for our staging environment; can we do a ramp schedule?
[08:01] Liam O'Connor: yes ramp from 10 rps up to 100 over 48 hours.
[08:08] Alex Rivera: what about data residency for test dataset — will it be uploaded to Redwood?
[08:13] Maya Chen: for private we can keep data inside your VPC; for hosted pilot you can sanize or use synthetic subset.
[08:22] Jonas Meier: any integration with our existing monitoring stack?
[08:26] Liam O'Connor: console exposes metrics and traces; we can push metrics to Prometheus or Datadog and traces to your tracing backend.
[08:35] Sara Delgado: i'm going to need the SOC2 and the KMS integration whitepaper.
[08:39] Maya Chen: yes — will attach links in the follow up.
[08:45] Mike Tan: legal will need sample terms.
[08:48] Maya Chen: noted, will include sample enterprise terms.
[08:52] Alex Rivera: ok final check: do we need any POC licenses or special GPU quota requests for the pilot?
[08:58] Liam O'Connor: we can allocate a small dedicated pool for the pilot, but quota depends on region capacity. i'd like to run a capacity check and we can propose burst options.
[09:10] Jonas Meier: who owns the SOW?
[09:13] Maya Chen: Redwood will draft initial SOW; Cerulean to review and propose edits.
[09:17] Alex Rivera: thanks, good session.
[09:20] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. quick recap in a sec.
[09:25] TRANSCRIPT AUTO-SUMMARY: "Cerulean Dataworks exploring Redwood private/dedicated options for hybrid GPU onramp. Key requirements: data residency, KMS BYOK, audit logs, p95 <400ms for 2k sequences. Next: security docs, SOW, perf bench."
[09:40] Maya Chen: recap: i'll send security pack and SOW draft; Liam will share perf spreadsheet and recommended configs; Alex will share dataset details and acceptance criteria. we aim to kick pilot week of 11/24.
[09:58] Alex Rivera: sounds good. thanks all.
[10:05] END OF TRANSCRIPT. Note: some audio dropped between 00:09:40 and 00:09:58 with short garble, minor mis-transcriptions ("dedikate"), speaker overlap.
